record_under_review.evidence_span: NeuroPDE uses probabilistic spin neurons to emulate random walks and non-volatile ferroelectric synapses for continuous weights in a neuromorphic PDE solver. For diffusion equations it reports variance below 1e-2 against analytical solutions, 3.48x–315x execution-time speedup, and 2.7x–29.8x energy advantage over advanced CMOS-based neuromorphic chips.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Emerging spintronic and ferroelectric devices with physical stochasticity and non-volatile analog weight storage; device models, variability, conversion, and fabrication assumptions require full-paper review.
record_under_review.limits: The preprint abstract does not expose PDE suite breadth, device-area and conversion costs, process assumptions, precision, or how CMOS baselines are normalized; ranges require paper-level verification.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: Neuromorphic architecture using stochastic spin neurons for probabilistic transmission and ferroelectric synapses for continuous non-volatile weights.
record_under_review.problem: Conventional von Neumann hardware lacks hardware-intrinsic randomness, limiting the performance of Monte Carlo and random-walk PDE solvers.
record_under_review.title: NeuroPDE: A Neuromorphic PDE Solver Based on Spintronic and Ferroelectric Devices
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Diffusion-equation PDE solving with comparison against analytical solutions and CMOS-based neuromorphic-chip baselines.
